target_customer: Employees at large employers who are not capturing their full 401(k) match or ESPP; employees pay a fee, employers do not
problem: About 1 in 4 workers miss their full employer 401(k) match because they cannot afford to contribute; Lendtable advances cash for living expenses so they can contribute and then takes part of the vested match.
business_model: Consumer cash advance repaid from vested employer match with a one-time fee (6% to 20% in 2020, 10% in later examples)
product_category: Fintech, retirement match and ESPP cash advances

founders.name: Sheridan Clayborne
education: Northwestern, computer science and economics (left to start company)
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page, which says he attended Northwestern at 15 and joined Dropbox at 19; the page claims over $5M raised and over $10M sales across past businesses (self-reported).

founders.name: Mitchell Jones
previous_startups: Parable (personal finance startup, per one search summary, outcome unknown)

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs employer plan data connections, underwriting against future vested match, and lending operations; standard fintech engineering with credit and compliance work.

defensibility.rationale: A niche lending product with plan data and repayment history, but little structural protection; lenders or earned wage access players could copy the concept.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of incumbents copying or buying it.

market_need_then: The company states 1 in 4 Americans do not capture their full 401(k) match, about $24 billion left on the table by 25 million workers (YC company page).

identity.visual_style: Not found; site fetch returned HTTP 402
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, benefit-led slogan 'we win if they win'

branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity TikTok creators Josh Richards, Bryce Hall and Griffin Johnson invested in the seed round (Tubefilter, 2020-10-01).

brand_strength.rationale: Creator and celebrity investors raised visibility at launch, and the name is easy to say, but it is close to Lendable and LendingClub and no evidence shows brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Lendtable launched in 2020 with a $3M seed backed by YC, SoftBank and Valor plus TikTok creators, then raised an $18M Series A in November 2021 led by O1 Advisors, bringing total venture funding to a reported $26M. It reported disbursing over $2.4M in match benefits by then. No news after 2021 was found, so later outcomes and current status are unknown.
notes: Total raised conflicts: Tubefilter says $4.5M after the seed, TPInsights says $26M after the Series A (so earlier funding of about $8M may be unrecorded), Seedtable lists $21M and a second report says $24M. The company website returned HTTP 402 so the site content was not read. Competitors named in the Series A article (Acorns, Betterment) are dated November 2021, well after the batch, and are described as paving the way rather than direct competition, so none are listed. Parable as a previous startup comes from a single search summary.
